messages:
oliver (acme-corp): Hey team — started hitting a crash when using the Python SDK in JSON mode with our streaming endpoint. It works for a while then the client raises ValueError: invalid literal for int() and the stream closes. Not sure if we changed something on our side.

emma (support): Sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact request/response snippets and SDK version? Also any stack trace from the client?

oliver (acme-corp): SDK 1.3.7. Repro is a streaming /v1/generate call with json_mode enabled. We stream tokens and expect top-level objects like: {
  "text": "...",
  "metadata": {"user_id": 123}  <-- optional for us, sometimes omitted
}
But intermittently the client fails when metadata is missing. Stack:

ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: ''
  File \"/usr/local/lib/python3.9/site-packages/redwood_sdk/stream.py\", line 210, in _handle_chunk
    item_id = int(m.group(1))

We capture raw frames and attached a small excerpt: 

--stream-frame-1--
data: {"text": "hello", "meta": null}

--stream-frame-2--
data: {"text": "more"}  <-- metadata omitted here

--stream-frame-3--
data: 

(empty line, then client crashes)

We suspect parser expects an id or numeric field in every frame.

emma (support): Thanks — filing a ticket. @maria from SDK team FYI. Can you take a look? I created ticket #INC-4892. support-bot: Ticket INC-4892 created and assigned to sdk-team.

maria (sdk): looking. thx for detailed repro. quick Q: are you using any proxy that might alter chunk boundaries? also can you confirm if you see any trailing commas or extra newlines in server frames?

oliver (acme-corp): No proxy, connecting directly. We see occasional empty data lines between frames (like frame-3 above). Happens more under high throughput (lots of small responses).

maria (sdk): I can reproduce locally with a small harness that simulates the server inserting an extra \n

Example repro snippet (python):
```py
from redwood import StreamingClient
c = StreamingClient(api_key=\"***\", json_mode=True)
with c.stream(\"/v1/generate\") as s:
    for chunk in s.iter_lines():
        print(repr(chunk))
```
Run against a fake server that yields: b'data: {"text":"a"}\n\n' then b'\n' then b'data: {"text":"b"}\n\n' — the iterator returns an empty string for the extra newline which our old int-parsing path tries to convert to an id.

Root cause theory: our streaming parser assumed every non-empty data line starts with an integer id token (legacy framing). When a blank line arrives (or a pure \"data:\" with empty payload), the regex group is empty and int() fails. This surfaces when optional fields cause the server to emit shorter frames that our chunker splits differently.

Workaround: upgrade to 1.3.8-beta or patch your client to ignore empty lines. Quick client-side fix:
```py
for chunk in s.iter_lines():
    if not chunk.strip():
        continue
    # existing parse path
```

raj (eng): adding context: we changed how optional metadata is emitted in the runtime to reduce token count (omits empty metadata object entirely). That increased instances of adjacent newlines on streaming boundary. SDK should be robust to empty frames. We'll patch the parser to skip blank data tokens and make the id parse resilient.

maria (sdk): created PR #sdk/122 that: 1) guards int() conversion with a check, 2) treats empty data lines as no-op, 3) adds unit tests for multiple-newline fragmentation. Plan to cut 1.3.8 release tomorrow PST.

oliver (acme-corp): thanks — tried local monkeypatch to skip blank lines and it stabilized the stream under load. Can you share ETA for release?

maria (sdk): aiming for a patch release in ~24 hours. I'll post the release notes and the temporary pip URL once available. Until publish, use the local guard or set json_mode to \"ndjson\" as a stopgap if switching server formatting is possible.

emma (support): i'll keep this ticket open and update customer on release. Oliver, let me know if you want an early wheel to test. :thumbsup:

oliver (acme-corp): yes please, an early wheel would be great. thanks for the fast turnaround.

maria (sdk): sending test wheel to your email in ~2 hours. follow-up: PR merged to staging and ci green. scheduled for release at 2026-03-18 18:00 UTC.

support-bot: INC-4892 status updated -> in-progress

oliver (acme-corp): verified the wheel, fixed the crash on our load test. closing on our side after we upgrade to 1.3.8. Appreciate the quick support!

emma (support): great — marking resolved from support side but leaving ticket for post-release monitoring. :white_check_mark:
